points.place: 弗吉尼亚州夏洛茨维尔
points.title: 早年教育
points.description: 托马斯·杰斐逊出生于弗吉尼亚州的富裕种植园主家庭。在威廉与玛丽学院学习期间，他受到教授威廉·斯莫尔的深刻影响，开始启蒙思想的学习。杰斐逊精通多种语言，包括法语、希腊语、拉丁语和意大利语，并广泛阅读哲学、科学和政治学著作。这段时期奠定了他一生对知识、自由和民主的坚定信念，为他后来的政治生涯和思想体系奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Born into a wealthy plantation family in Virginia, Jefferson received his early education at the College of William and Mary, where he was deeply influenced by Professor William Small. During this period, he mastered multiple languages including French, Greek, Latin, and Italian, and extensively read philosophy, science, and political works. This formative period established his lifelong commitment to knowledge, liberty, and democracy, laying the foundation for his later political career and philosophical system.

points.title: 法律实践与政治启蒙
points.description: 杰斐逊在威廉斯堡开始律师生涯，迅速成为弗吉尼亚殖民地最成功的律师之一。1774年，他撰写了《英属美洲权利概观》，抨击英国对殖民地的税收政策，主张殖民地权利。1776年，作为弗吉尼亚代表参加大陆会议，他起草了《独立宣言》，确立了'人人生而平等'和'不可剥夺的权利'等原则。这一时期，他还起草了弗吉尼亚宗教自由法案，主张政教分离，这些思想成为美国宪政的重要基石。
points.descriptionEn: Beginning his legal career in Williamsburg, Jefferson quickly became one of Virginia's most successful attorneys. In 1774, he authored 'Summary View of the Rights of British America,' criticizing British taxation policies and asserting colonial rights. In 1776, as Virginia's delegate to the Continental Congress, he drafted the Declaration of Independence, establishing principles such as 'all men are created equal' and 'unalienable rights.' During this period, he also drafted the Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom, advocating separation of church and state, which became cornerstones of American constitutionalism.

points.title: 外交使节
points.description: 作为美国驻法外交使节，杰斐逊在巴黎度过了关键五年。他深受法国启蒙思想影响，与伏尔泰、狄德罗等哲学家交往密切。1784-1786年间，他与约翰·亚当斯和本杰明·富兰克林共同谈判美国与法国之间的商业条约。这段经历极大地拓展了他的国际视野，使他认识到民主制度的全球意义。同时，他对法国大革命持同情态度，认为这是美国革命理想的延伸，这种国际视野影响了他后来的外交政策理念。
points.descriptionEn: As American diplomatic envoy to France, Jefferson spent five crucial years in Paris. Deeply influenced by French Enlightenment thought, he closely associated with philosophers like Voltaire and Diderot. Between 1784-1786, he negotiated commercial treaties between the United States and France alongside John Adams and Benjamin Franklin. This experience significantly broadened his international perspective, leading him to recognize the global significance of democratic systems. He sympathized with the French Revolution, viewing it as an extension of American revolutionary ideals, which influenced his later foreign policy concepts.

points.title: 国务卿时期
points.description: 作为首任美国国务卿，杰斐逊与财政部长汉密尔顿之间形成了激烈的意识形态对立。杰斐逊主张农业社会、有限政府和严格解释宪法，而汉密尔顿则支持工业发展、强大中央政府和灵活解释宪法。这种分歧导致了美国第一个政党系统的形成，杰斐逊成为民主共和党的领袖。他反对汉密尔顿的金融政策，认为这会过度增强联邦政府权力，损害各州权利。这一时期的思想对立奠定了美国两党政治的基础，也塑造了杰斐逊的政治哲学。
points.descriptionEn: As the first U.S. Secretary of State, Jefferson formed a fierce ideological opposition with Treasury Secretary Hamilton. Jefferson advocated for an agrarian society, limited government, and strict constitutional interpretation, while Hamilton supported industrial development, strong central government, and flexible constitutional interpretation. This division led to the formation of America's first party system, with Jefferson becoming the leader of the Democratic-Republican Party. He opposed Hamilton's financial policies, believing they would excessively strengthen federal power at the expense of states' rights. This ideological conflict laid the foundation for American two-party politics and shaped Jefferson's political philosophy.

points.title: 总统任期
points.description: 作为美国第三任总统，杰斐逊的任期标志着美国民主共和党政治理念的实践。1803年，他主导了路易斯安那购地，使美国领土扩大近一倍，尽管这超越了宪法赋予他的权力。他削减政府开支，降低国债，推行'勤俭政府'政策。在外交方面，他成功处理了巴巴里海盗问题，避免了与欧洲主要强国的战争。杰斐逊还签署了1807年《禁运法案》，试图保持美国中立，但这一政策反而导致经济困难。他的总统任期体现了理想主义与现实政治的平衡，对美国民主制度的发展产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: As the third U.S. president, Jefferson's term marked the practical implementation of Democratic-Republican political ideals. In 1803, he orchestrated the Louisiana Purchase, nearly doubling U.S. territory despite exceeding his constitutional authority. He reduced government spending, lowered the national debt, and promoted policies of 'frugal government.' Diplomatically, he successfully addressed the Barbary pirates issue while avoiding war with major European powers. Jefferson also signed the Embargo Act of 1807, attempting to maintain U.S. neutrality, though this policy反而 caused economic difficulties. His presidency balanced idealism with practical politics, profoundly influencing the development of American democratic institutions.

points.place: 弗吉尼亚州夏洛茨维尔
points.title: 晚年与遗产
points.description: 退休后，杰斐逊回到蒙蒂塞洛，专注于学术和教育活动。他创建了弗吉尼亚大学，设计了校园建筑并亲自制定课程，这成为他最引以为傲的成就之一。杰斐逊与约翰·亚当斯恢复通信，两人晚年重新建立了友谊，这些信件成为美国早期政治思想的重要文献。1826年7月4日，独立宣言签署50周年之际，杰斐逊逝世，享年83岁。他一生拥有数百名奴隶，这一矛盾成为他遗产中的复杂部分。杰斐逊去世后，他的政治理念、教育思想和民主理想继续影响着美国政治发展，成为美国民主制度的重要象征。
points.descriptionEn: In retirement, Jefferson returned to Monticello, focusing on academic and educational pursuits. He founded the University of Virginia, designing its campus architecture and personally developing its curriculum, which he considered one of his proudest achievements. Jefferson renewed his friendship with John Adams in their later years, with their correspondence becoming important documents of early American political thought. On July 4, 1826, the 50th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, Jefferson died at age 83. His lifelong ownership of hundreds of slaves remains a complex aspect of his legacy. After his death, his political philosophy, educational ideals, and democratic vision continued to influence American political development, making him an enduring symbol of American democracy.

appraisal.zh: 杰斐逊通常被视为美国民主制度的主要奠基者之一，《独立宣言》中「人人生而平等」的理念、对宗教自由与公共教育的倡导，以及路易斯安那购地和创办弗吉尼亚大学，都深刻塑造了美国的宪政与民主进程。但另一种看法认为，他的遗产充满矛盾：他终身蓄奴，宣言中的平等把奴隶、妇女和原住民排除在外，禁运法案损害经济，州权主张后来被用于维护奴隶制，对农业社会的理想化也延缓了现代化。
appraisal.en: Jefferson is generally regarded as a principal founder of American democracy: the idea that 'all men are created equal' in the Declaration of Independence, his advocacy of religious freedom and public education, the Louisiana Purchase, and the founding of the University of Virginia all deeply shaped American constitutional and democratic development. Another view holds that his legacy is riddled with contradictions: he owned slaves throughout his life, his equality excluded slaves, women, and Native Americans, the Embargo Act damaged the economy, his states' rights doctrine was later used to defend slavery, and his idealization of an agrarian society slowed modernization.

supporter.zh: 杰斐逊被视为美国民主制度的奠基人之一，他的政治理念塑造了美国宪政的核心原则。《独立宣言》中'人人生而平等'的理念成为美国民主的基石，他对宗教自由、教育普及和有限政府的倡导影响了后世。作为总统，他通过路易斯安那购地大幅扩展了美国领土，建立了民主共和党，为美国两党政治奠定了基础。杰斐逊创立的弗吉尼亚大学体现了他对知识的热爱和对公共教育的重视，他的思想遗产至今仍影响着美国的民主进程。
supporter.en: Jefferson is regarded as one of the founders of American democracy, whose political philosophy shaped the core principles of American constitutionalism. The concept of 'all men are created equal' in the Declaration of Independence became the cornerstone of American democracy, and his advocacy for religious freedom, public education, and limited government influenced future generations. As president, he significantly expanded U.S. territory through the Louisiana Purchase, established the Democratic-Republican Party, and laid the foundation for America's two-party system. The University of Virginia, which he founded, reflects his love of knowledge and commitment to public education, and his philosophical legacy continues to influence America's democratic process.

critic.zh: 杰斐逊的遗产充满矛盾，他一方面倡导自由平等，另一方面终身拥有奴隶，与多名女奴发生关系并育有子女。他的'人人生而平等'宣言排除了奴隶、妇女和原住民，体现了当时的社会局限性。作为总统，他签署的《禁运法案》导致经济困难，损害了美国商业利益。他的州权主张在后来被南方奴隶州用来维护奴隶制，成为分裂国家的因素之一。杰斐逊对农业社会的理想化忽视了工业发展的必要性，这种思想在一定程度上延缓了美国的现代化进程。
critic.en: Jefferson's legacy is marked by profound contradictions. While advocating for liberty and equality, he was a lifelong slave owner who had relationships with enslaved women and fathered children with them. His 'all men are created equal' declaration excluded slaves, women, and Native Americans, reflecting the social limitations of his time. As president, the Embargo Act he signed caused economic hardship and damaged American commercial interests. His states' rights advocacy was later used by Southern slave states to defend slavery, becoming a factor in national division. Jefferson's idealization of an agrarian society overlooked the necessity of industrial development, potentially slowing America's modernization process.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，杰斐逊被视为美国历史上最具影响力的思想家和政治家之一，同时也是最具争议的人物。他的思想既被自由主义者引用，也被保守者解读；既被用来支持民权运动，也被用来维护现状。杰斐逊的蒙蒂塞洛故居成为美国历史地标，他的形象出现在美元硬币和总统山上，成为美国国家认同的象征。现代学者通过研究他的生平和著作，试图理解美国建国理念中的理想与现实之间的张力，以及民主制度如何在矛盾中发展。杰斐逊的复杂性和多面性使他成为美国历史研究中永恒的课题。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Jefferson is regarded as one of the most influential thinkers and statesmen in American history, yet also one of the most controversial figures. His ideas have been invoked by both liberals and conservatives, used to support civil rights movements and to defend the status quo. Monticello, his home, has become a historical landmark, and his image appears on currency and Mount Rushmore, symbolizing American national identity. Modern scholars study his life and writings to understand the tension between ideals and reality in America's founding principles, and how democratic institutions develop amid contradictions. Jefferson's complexity and multifaceted nature make him an enduring subject of American historical research.

self.zh: 我相信这个国家的未来将取决于它在多大程度上运用和实施这些原则。
self.en: I believe that this nation's future will depend upon how much it applies and implements these principles.
